newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Twenty-three in hospital after Gulf Air accident.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-three in hospital after Gulf Air accident.

text.p: Twenty-three of the people onboard a Gulf Air Airbus that aborted takeoff from Abu Dhabi airport on Monday remain hospitalised, the official WAM news agency said on Tuesday.
It said doctors at a hospital where they are being treated said they were in good health.
The British pilot and several other people aboard the aircraft were injured when he aborted a takeoff.

The front wheel came off the A-320, which was on a flight to Cairo via Bahrain, sending the nose skidding along the runway, the civil aviation authority said. The 107 passengers and eight crew were evacuated.

WAM said Sheikh Ahmed bin Saif al-Nahayan, deputy head of the Abu Dhabi civil aviation authority and Gulf Air chief executive, on Tuesday visited the hospitalised passengers from the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Sudan, England, Holland, Lebanon, Bahrain and the Philippines.
Sheikh Ahmed said the pilot, who sustained the most serious injuries, was being treated in the intensive care unit and was in stable condition.
He said it was too early to comment on the cause of the crash and that a technical commitee had been formed to investigate the incident.
A company statement said 77 passengers had left hospital after completing medical examinations.
"Ten more passengers left the hospital today (Tuesday) and only 28 passengers are still receiving medical care," the statement said. It did not elaborate.
Bahrain-based Gulf Air is jointly owned by the governments of Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar.
